page: Microsoft Azure E16pds_v7 is an ARM-based memory-optimized virtual machine instance running on Microsoft Hyper-V. It is configured with 16 dedicated arm64 vCPUs and 128.0 GB of memory, yielding an 8:1 memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. Storage capabilities include a bundled 945 GB local NVMe SSD drive alongside support for Premium Storage. The instance does not include GPU accelerators and provides no complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

By utilizing ARM architecture, the instance provides high compute and memory density, resulting in resource and power efficiencies for scale-out workloads. A primary tradeoff involves instruction architecture, requiring workloads to support arm64 rather than x86 extensions. The bundled 945 GB NVMe storage offers low latency for scratch space, temporary indexing, and caching, though persistent data retention depends on auxiliary remote storage.

This balance of dedicated compute cores, large memory capacity, and high-speed local disk accommodates memory-heavy tasks. Suitable workloads include in-memory databases, distributed caching layers, relational database servers, extract-transform-load (ETL) pipelines, and memory-constrained data science jobs.
description: Microsoft Azure E16pds_v7 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance running on Microsoft Hyper-V with an arm64 architecture. It provides 16 dedicated vCPUs and 128.0 GB of system memory, establishing an 8.0 GB per vCPU allocation. The hardware configuration includes 945 GB of bundled local NVMe SSD storage and supports Premium Storage features. The instance contains no discrete GPU processors and does not provide complimentary public IPv4 addresses. Leveraging ARM processor architecture enables favorable resource efficiency and compute density for multithreaded processing, provided target applications are compiled for ARM. The integrated NVMe volume facilitates high-throughput scratch data access and ephemeral caching. These specifications make the E16pds_v7 instance well aligned with enterprise workloads requiring substantial memory and rapid local disk access, including relational databases, in-memory key-value stores, real-time analytics engines, and intermediate data processing pipelines.
